messages:
maria (Support): heads-up — customer 'AcmeChat' just hit a spike after today's rate policy push and they're seeing lots of 429s + weird billing deltas. they reported user-facing errors and increased latency. i tried a quick repro and saw a sawtooth pattern in errors

maria (Support): error sample from their logs: `POST /v1/generate 429` with header `x-rate-limit-retry-after: 15` but client says retry-after varies wildly per request. also billing micro-charges kept increasing even for 429s :/

tom (eng-platform): thanks for flagging. which rollout id did we use for the policy? i think this was the partial push to 40% earlier today. deploy-bot should have the record

deploy-bot: rollout finished: rate-policy-v3 -> 40% of prod at 1972500900 (canary window open). no automated rollback triggered.

anya (eng-sre): saw a similar pattern on internal telemetry — a burst of small requests from a few IPs caused the rate-controller to oscillate, leading to rapid quota depletion + token accounting glitches. could explain sawtooth.

devon (eng-oncall): can you paste the customer's request fingerprint? i want to check gateway logs and the rate limiter decisions. also need to know if this is per-api-key or per-tenant quota


maria (Support): customer supplied api_key: acme-xxx-123. requests are short chat completions with small token counts but very high RPS bursts. they say it started ~12:03 UTC when they resumed a job.

linda (customer-success): i'm on standby with the customer. they want a fast rollback if it's our config. please call out what we'll tell them.

tom (eng-platform): initial mitigation options: 1) stop the staged rollout (set canary to 0%) 2) temporarily raise per-key burst window for acme-xxx-123 3) rollback to rate-policy-v2. preference order depends on blast radius.

anya (eng-sre): quick triage steps i recommend now: 
- check gateway decisions: `grep acme-xxx-123 /var/log/gateway/requests.log | tail -n 200`
- inspect limiter metrics: `promql: rate_limit_evicts_total{policy=\"rate-policy-v3\"}`
- confirm billing pipeline: are 429ed requests being billed? check `billing_events_in_window` for that key

maria (Support): i ran tail on logs and saw both `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` and occasional `X-RateLimit-Remaining: -1` entries — negative remaining looks bad. forwarded sample to eng.

maria (Support): also the customer captured a curl repro. sharing: ```
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer acme-xxx-123\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"input\":\"hi\"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -v
```

devon (eng-oncall): negative remaining likely a bookkeeping bug during concurrent decrement + refill. could be a race in the token bucket implementation when switching policies mid-flight.

tom (eng-platform): ok i'm going to pause the canary. doing: `rctl rollout update --name=rate-policy-v3 --percent=0 --reason=\"pause after acme surge\"` will stop further traffic shifts. doing it now.

deploy-bot: rollout update accepted: rate-policy-v3 -> 0% at 1972501402 by tom (eng-platform).

anya (eng-sre): while that's happening i'll check the limiter state and resume a patch to avoid negative counters. possible quick fix: clamp remaining at min 0 in response headers and avoid billing events for requests that are 429'd.

tom (eng-platform): agree on clamping header as bandaid, but long term we need to ensure billing pipeline uses canonical ack from router not header delta. i'll open a ticket.

maria (Support): customer is asking for ETA and whether we can do a rollback to v2. linda is with them.

linda (customer-success): customer is pushing for rollback now, their users are impacted. want to know if rollback is safe w.r.t. data integrity

devon (eng-oncall): rollback to v2 should be safe — config only. but confirm no schema changes in v3. if all green, we can pin them to v2 at tenant level: `rctl tenant-config set --tenant=acme --rate-policy=rate-policy-v2`

tom (eng-platform): i'll prepare tenant pin and global rollback. plan: 1) pin acme to v2 now 2) global rollback if we see other customers affected 3) follow-up hotfix for negative remaining.

anya (eng-sre): i'm seeing the limiter logs: concurrent refill tasks tried to reconcile local token state with central quota and produced transient negative counters when vote lost. patch candidate: atomically read-modify-write with CAS. i'll create PR and a hotfix release.

maria (Support): customer update sent: \"we see requests succeed again for a short while then drop — looks unstable\". they asked if we disabled anything.

tom (eng-platform): pinned acme to v2 at 1972501530. command: `rctl tenant-config set --tenant=acme --rate-policy=rate-policy-v2 --apply-now`

deploy-bot: tenant config updated: acme -> rate-policy-v2 at 1972501530 by tom.

devon (eng-oncall): confirm on gateway logs — after pinning some success, saw steady calls w/o negative remaining. still want to watch for billing events. please hold billing adjustments until we confirm window.

linda (customer-success): told customer we pinned them and are investigating root cause. they asked for an incident postmortem and a timeline for fix. i'll schedule a 1:1 after we stabilize.

anya (eng-sre): PR will be up in ~20m. hotfix plan: rollback-safe patch to limiter, CI run, canary to 5% for 15m, then promote. will coordinate with platform for a controlled rollout.

tom (eng-platform): agreed. timeline: pause done, acme pinned, hotfix -> canary 5% -> monitor 30m -> promote. if errors reappear, full rollback global. i'll coordinate rollout window and notify support before any promote.

maria (Support): thanks team. i'll keep the customer updated and log the repro artifacts. please @maria when the canary 5% is up so i can tell them. :thumbsup:

devon (eng-oncall): adding note — mitigate billing by marking 429 events with internal flag `no_charge=true` until we verify. tom can you confirm the billing gate?

tom (eng-platform): will add a safe-check in billing pipeline to ignore events where `response_code >= 400 && response_code != 200 && no_charge=true`. i'll put in a short-lived rule and revert after postmortem.

linda (customer-success): customer appreciates the quick pin. keep me posted on the hotfix timeline so i can block meetings for them.

maria (Support): final for now — created support ticket SUP-4821 and attached their curl output and logs. will update thread with any new customer feedback.

anya (eng-sre): PR link: https://git.redwood/repo/limiter/compare/fix-negative-counters (draft). running unit + stress tests now.

tom (eng-platform): thanks all. follow-ups: 1) eng-sre to land hotfix and canary 5% 2) platform to add billing guard 3) support to gather repros 4) cs to notify customer timeline. we'll reconvene on this thread for promote/rollback decision.

maria (Support): acknowledged.

deploy-bot: scheduled canary: limiter-fix -> 5% at 1972502100 (awaiting manual trigger by eng-platform).

maria (Support): marking this thread as the coordination channel for the issue.
